Built Here. For Here.

The people who grow wheat deserve the same intelligence the trading desks take for granted.

MarketBullets was founded in the heart of Pacific Northwest soft white wheat country — north of Prescott, Washington — by someone who grew up in this landscape, who knows what it costs when you get the marketing decision wrong, and who spent four decades building a better way to read the market before it moves.

The commentary integrates verified USDA and CFTC data, proprietary technical frameworks, and global supply context spanning Black Sea logistics to Pacific Rim demand — synthesized into a coherent stance on where the market is and what it may do next.

The analysis is built on a simple premise: producers, merchandisers, landlords, and lenders who make real pricing decisions deserve institutional-quality market intelligence.

“More Sense Per Bushel isn’t a tagline. It’s a daily standard.”

Legacy

The boots get smaller.The stakes get higher.

Your grandfather didn’t lose the farm in a drought. Your father didn’t lose it in a bad year. The risk isn’t in the weather anymore — it’s in the marketing decision made without the right information, in the wrong week, at the wrong price, with no one in your corner who’s seen this pattern before.

Every bushel represents choices made generations ago, sacrifices your parents endured, and dreams you’re building for kids who might not even be born yet. When you’re watching prices, you’re not just protecting margins — you’re protecting legacy.

MarketBullets exists because those decisions deserve better than a guess.

The Chart Gallery

60 instruments. Five chapters.

Every chart in the member dashboard exists for a reason. Here’s what each category tells you — and why it matters to your marketing decision.

14

Wheat Futures

The primary destination every morning. Chicago SRW, Kansas City HRW, Minneapolis HRS, and Paris Milling Wheat — daily, weekly, and continuous contract views that show where each market is, where it’s been, and what the technical structure suggests.

ZW · KE · MWE · EBM · continuation charts · seasonal overlays

Why it’s the foundation

“Before I can tell you what to do, I need to know where each contract stands relative to its own history. These charts are the foundation. Everything else is context.”

23

Spreads & Ratios

The relationships between markets often signal what flat price misses. Class spreads, crop-year spreads, wheat-to-corn ratios — structural tensions that reveal direction before they resolve in price movement.

SRW–HRW · HRW–HRS · wheat/corn ratio · old crop/new crop · calendar spreads

What the spread tells you

When the SRW/HRW spread compresses or widens unusually, something is shifting in the supply picture. Spreads are the market’s internal conversation — and most producers never listen to it.

6

Currencies

The U.S. Dollar Index is the single most important correlated market for wheat exporters. A strong dollar makes American wheat less competitive globally. Six currency charts track the dollar against major trading partners.

DXY · EUR/USD · USD/RUB · AUD/USD · BRL/USD · CAD/USD

The dollar’s mood affects your basis

DXY above 100 is a headwind. Below 100, a tailwind. Watching it daily keeps you from being surprised when export sales disappoint — or exceed — expectations.

4

Interest Rates

High Treasury yields pressure commodity prices through multiple channels — stronger dollar, higher carry costs, reduced speculative appetite. Four charts track the rate environment that sets the macro backdrop for every wheat trade.

10-Year Treasury · 2-Year Treasury · yield curve · Fed Funds implied rate

Macro pressure, made visible

When the yield curve inverts or the 10-year spikes, commodity markets often follow. Knowing the rate environment helps you understand why wheat is behaving as it is — even on days when nothing in the grain world has changed.

13

General Macro

Crude oil, gold, the S&P 500, the Baltic Dry Index — the systemic forces that shape commodity market sentiment, input costs, and global trade economics. These charts tell you whether money is flowing toward or away from real assets.

WTI crude · gold · S&P 500 · Baltic Dry · natural gas · VIX · global equities

The world beyond the grain pit

Risk-on environments support commodities. Risk-off drains them. Knowing which environment you’re in — through gold, equities, and crude — changes how you interpret every wheat price move that follows.

The Signal System

Box-o-Rox:
Four phases. One clear stance.

Box-o-Rox is the sell/suspend signal component within The Warm Signal (TWS) — a proprietary framework built over 44 years of wheat market pattern recognition. The name is a deliberate provocation: effective signals don’t need to be complex. They need to be right.

The system tracks Chicago SRW price relative to its 60-day moving average and moves through four phases. Each phase defines a marketing posture — not a price target, not a guarantee, but a stance built on historical pattern convergence.

PHASE I

Loaded

Accumulation. Market below the 60-day MA. Patience is the posture. Watch, don’t sell.

PHASE II

Locked & Loaded

Setup complete. Technical structure aligned. The coil is wound. Confirmation pending.

PHASE III

Aim

Signal confirmation. Pattern converged. Final check before the marketing trigger fires.

PHASE IV

Fire

Execution. The signal has fired. This is the window. Sell, price, or take protective action.

From the desk of Gary Hofer  ·  Waitsburg, Washington

Dear Wheat Producer,

I built MarketBullets because I got tired of watching good farmers make bad marketing decisions — not from ignorance, but from information poverty. The same data that moves the market is available to everyone. The pattern recognition that makes it useful is not.

Forty-four years of watching these markets has taught me that price doesn’t move randomly. It moves in patterns shaped by supply fundamentals, managed money positioning, seasonal tendencies, and correlated market forces. Those patterns can be read. They can be communicated clearly, with sources named and implications drawn. And when they are, they change what you do.

That’s the promise of MarketBullets®. Not a price target. Not a guarantee. The same quality of market intelligence institutional trading desks take for granted — built in wheat country, for wheat country. When you make that call to your elevator, you’ll know why.

More Sense Per Bushel.

Gary Hofer

Founder & Analyst, MarketBullets®  ·  Waitsburg, Washington  ·  44 Years Pacific Northwest Wheat Markets
